title: Below 1.0.0 the bump severity shifts down one level
expectation: A release that has not reached 1.0.0 shifts each severity down one level, because pre-1.0 consumers read every release as potentially breaking: a `minor` change on 0.4.2 plans 0.4.3, not 0.5.0, and a `major` change plans 0.5.0, not 1.0.0. Above 1.0.0 the same changes behave normally. The dependent crate follows through dependency propagation in both cases.

checks.command:
rm -f .changeset/*.md; mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
acme-util: minor
---

Add a helper
' > .changeset/grader-minor.md; monochange preview --format json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); t={x['id']: x['version'] for x in d['release_targets']}; assert t.get('acme-util')=='0.4.3', t; assert t.get('acme-tool')=='0.4.3', t; print(t)"; j=$?; rm -f .changeset/grader-minor.md; exit $j
checks.why: The shift is easy to mistake for a bug and easy to 'fix' by accident. On 0.4.2 a minor must move the patch position; a plan of 0.5.0 would mean the shift was dropped.

checks.command:
rm -f .changeset/*.md; mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
acme-util: major
---

Break the API
' > .changeset/grader-major.md; monochange preview --format json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); t={x['id']: x['version'] for x in d['release_targets']}; assert t.get('acme-util')=='0.5.0', t; print(t)"; j=$?; rm -f .changeset/grader-major.md; exit $j
checks.why: The upper half of the same rule: a breaking change on 0.x moves the minor position rather than jumping to 1.0.0, because reaching 1.0.0 is a deliberate product decision rather than something a severity chooses.

checks.command:
cp crates/util/Cargo.toml .util.bak; python3 -c "import pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('crates/util/Cargo.toml'); p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('version = "0.4.2"', 'version = "1.4.2"'))"; rm -f .changeset/*.md; mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
acme-util: minor
---

Add a helper
' > .changeset/grader-minor.md; monochange preview --format json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); t={x['id']: x['version'] for x in d['release_targets']}; assert t.get('acme-util')=='1.5.0', t; print(t)"; j=$?; mv .util.bak crates/util/Cargo.toml; rm -f .changeset/grader-minor.md; exit $j
checks.why: The counterpart that makes the rule a rule rather than a constant: at 1.4.2 the same minor change must move the minor position. Without this, a fix that shifted every version would still pass the two checks above.
